Q: How to disable GSM Modem unsolicited SMS arrival message? A:

I've seen some answers over the internet like here:

AT+CNMI=0,0,0,0,0

But actually it should be this: (read the AT commands reference!)

AT+CNMI=1,0,0,0,0

This means that 'mode' is set to '1' = Discard indication.

A couple of pitfalls: 1) if you are using CMUX mode, then execute this command on your 'AT' dlc channel (usually dlci 0 is a system one, dlci 1 is for ppp (as it is commonly the only one to have large buffer), dlci 2 for AT commands (like checking GSM network state, signal level, etc)). 2) If you're using PDU mode, then it may be necessary first to switch mode to 'text', execute CNMI, and then switch back to PDU and execute CNMI again. 3) Even using CNMI this way, I still get unsolicited CMT during establishing ppp connection. But after the ppp is established, there are no unsolicited CMT messages.

Tested with SimCom A7602E modem.

UPD:

This CNMI turned out to be much trickier than it seemed to be. Eventually I managed things to work by just setting up storage location (all three mems point to modem's memory), setting up PDU mode and finally:

AT+CNMI=1,1,0,0,0

And seems now that it is no matter when to issue these commands: on the main UART, on CMUX'ed UART or on any other. Note that DTR must be set off:

AT&D0

Q: Calculating percentages for discrete values entered in an Excel column A:

As a slight variation on @Scott Craner's nice answer, you can also do the percentage inside the groupby =LET(RNG,Table1[Value],GROUPBY(RNG,RNG,LAMBDA(x,COUNTA(x)/COUNTA(RNG)),0,0))
